headline: Finnish and European grid-scale battery storage keeps moving from permitting to construction, while hydrogen support is concentrating on fewer projects and the EU grids rules are still unfinished.
outlook_reason: Storage installs are growing fast, several 250-300 MWh Finnish projects started construction in autumn 2026 and Horizon calls for batteries, long-duration storage and digital grids open from December 2026, though grids legislation and hydrogen delivery remain uncertain.

metrics.label: European storage forecast 2030 (SolarPower Europe, medium)
metrics.value: 138 GWh, 28% CAGR 2026-30; EUPD Research expects 57 GWh in 2026

metrics.label: Finland grid storage capacity (Fingrid)
metrics.value: about 1,050 MW (980 MW from 261 systems of 1 MW or more, plus about 70 MW smaller)

metrics.label: Finland storage capacity (Renewables Finland)
metrics.value: just over 1.6 GW operating, nearly 1 GW under construction, 11.9 GW planned (definition differs from Fingrid)

metrics.value: about EUR 1.09 billion to 9 projects, about 1.1 GW electrolysis; bid range EUR 0.57-3.49/kg per Hydrogen Europe

signals.title: Nala Renewables starts construction on 125 MW / 250 MWh Vuolijoki BESS
signals.detail: Notice to proceed issued for one of the largest BESS projects in Finland to start construction; it follows Nala's purchase of ready-to-build projects from Finnish developers such as Fu-Gen.

signals.title: Delta Capacity starts 125 MW / 300 MWh Kärppiö BESS with Sungrow
signals.detail: Second Delta project under construction after AKKU One in Lapinlahti. Commissioning is planned for Q4 2027.

signals.title: EU Council adopts general approach on the European Grids Package
signals.detail: Parliament's position is not confirmed and trilogues are expected. Industry groups say the Council underplays storage and flexibility as alternatives to grid build-out. A first tripartite agreement on storage was signed alongside it. Status needs checking against official sources.

signals.title: Third European Hydrogen Bank auction results published
signals.detail: About EUR 1.09 billion for 9 projects. Finland's Vetyalfa (Cloudberry, 500 MW) won in the low-carbon topic. Reported bid prices differ between sources. This is an older item, added as context for the hydrogen gap in the first run.

signals.title: Only six second-round Hydrogen Bank winners sign grants
signals.detail: Six projects (380 MW) signed, including Finnish ones. This shows delivery risk for hydrogen subsidies. Older item, kept as context.
